notes: From Miami, with the BEAT the HEAT tour on the road to BANNED in the US. The broadcast recaps BattleBRAWL 2. Victoria Hawke beats Carlee Marx, Steven Shane beats HAL, Cameron Cruise beats John Doe to become Television Championship number-one contender, and MWG takes the PRODIGY© Classic Xtreme Championship from Chaos in a Christmas Tree Death Match. Juliet Marceau hires a young woman named Natalie and sends her to look for a vanished former champion. In the main event Foxx and Felicia Hart beat Caitlyn Daymon and Women's Champion Karla Starr.

matches.note: Karla Starr retains with the Morning Starr, a top-rope moonsault, after the returning Caitlyn Daymon hits Foxx with a steel chair and an inverted DDT while the referee is down.

Chaos picks the stipulation: 250 fluorescent tubes in and around the ring, and above it a scaffold with a barbed-wire spiderweb two feet below it. Larry Tact wins when he drops a frog splash from the roof of the scaffold onto Chaos and both fall through the spiderweb to the ring; Chaos keeps the PRODIGY© Classic Xtreme Championship. Juliet Marceau is at ringside on commentary.

matches.note: Twenty men, a new entrant every two minutes. Shawn Hart enters at number one and lasts one hour and thirty-eight minutes; Steven Shane debuts at number twenty. The entry order was Hart, Steve Johnson, Ulysis Solian, MWG, Chris McMillan, Mr. Entertainment, Copycat, Tommy O'Hagan, Joey Melton, Alister Hayze, JR White, Cameron Cruise, Daymon, Luscious, Jason Payne, Trevor Cane, HAL, Ozeki, John Doe and Steven Shane. Hart and Daymon, the last two, go over the top rope together; Marcus LaRoque rules from the video that Daymon's feet touched the floor first and Hart is the winner, and promises Daymon a championship shot of his own.

notes: New ERA's fourth pay-per-view and its second BattleBRAWL, the first pay-per-view in over a year. Karla Starr retains the Women's Championship over Foxx, Larry Tact beats Chaos in the first and probably last 250 Lighttube Circus Death Match, Shawn Hart wins the twenty-man BattleBRAWL rumble from the number-one spot, and Jonathan Marx retains the World Heavyweight Championship over the Phantom Republican. Open to wrestlers from any promotion, the rumble includes Ulysis Solian, Copycat and Joey Melton, who are not on New ERA's roster. Dean Julius arrives at the broadcast table partway through.
